summary: This section allows the Central Government to free certain groups of foreign companies from the rules of this chapter. It does this by publishing an official notice called a notification. A copy of this notice must also be shown to both Houses of Parliament.
points: The Central Government can exempt classes of foreign companies from Chapter rules.
This applies to companies already incorporated or to be incorporated outside India.
It applies regardless of whether the company has or will have a place of business in India.
The exemption must be done through an official notification specifying the details.
A copy of the notification must be placed before both Houses of Parliament.
example: Global Tech Corp is a business incorporated outside India that plans to open a local office in India. The Central Government issues an official notification stating that a specific group of foreign companies, which includes businesses like Global Tech Corp, does not need to follow certain rules found in this chapter. To ensure transparency, the government places a copy of this notification before both Houses of Parliament shortly after it is made.

terms.meaning: Companies or bodies corporate incorporated outside India.
An official public announcement or notice issued by the government.

watch: Do not assume all foreign companies are automatically freed from the rules, as an official government notification is required.
